A new therapeutic concept for opioid administration has been proposed as Patient-Controlled Therapy (PCT) of breathlessness in palliative care. This approach involves allowing patients to control their own opioid doses under the guidance of healthcare professionals, with the goal of reducing refractory breathlessness.

The idea is that by giving patients more autonomy and flexibility in managing their opioid therapy, they may be able to better cope with their symptoms and improve their quality of life. This can also help reduce the risk of adverse effects associated with long-term opioid use.

Studies have shown that this approach can be effective in reducing breathlessness in palliative care patients. By providing patients with a sense of control and agency over their treatment, healthcare professionals can help them navigate the complexities of opioid therapy and make informed decisions about their own care.

Overall, PCT of breathlessness in palliative care represents an innovative approach to addressing this complex and challenging issue. It has the potential to improve patient outcomes, reduce costs, and enhance the overall quality of life for patients with severe respiratory conditions.
